  "title": "Static Geometry, Dynamic Failure: Mechanistic Decomposition of Character-Level Counting Degradation Under Extended Reasoning",
  "core_problem": "The counting failure literature has rapidly converged on three mechanistically distinct explanations for why LLMs fail at character-level tasks despite internally representing the correct answer. First, Garcia (2605.03258) demonstrates a static geometric readout bottleneck: count-encoding directions in residual streams are nearly orthogonal to digit-token output-head rows (|cos| ≤ 0.032 across Pythia, Qwen3, Mistral 0.4B–14B), so the model computes the correct count (linear probe R² > 0.99) but cannot project it through the output head (logit-lens accuracy peaks at 23.4%). Second, Datta et al. (2604.00778) and the Repeated-Token Counting study (2605.09239) identify active late-layer MLP suppression at 88–93% network depth that overwrites correctly-encoded counts in a format-triggered manner—space-separated lists trigger suppression while comma-separated lists can rescue it. Third, Garcia's logit-lens trajectory reveals that layers ~20–26 attempt to route count information toward output-compatible directions (accuracy rises from ~0% to 41.6%), and his LoRA Q/V attention fix (7.67M params, 83.1% ± 7.2% accuracy) proves this fragile attention routing compensation channel exists but is insufficient alone.

Separately, SubTokenTest (2601.09089) documented an inverted U-shaped curve where reasoning model performance on character-level tasks peaks at ~2048 thinking tokens then significantly degrades, and Gema et al. (2507.14417, TMLR 2025) independently confirmed inverse scaling on counting tasks with distractors under extended test-time compute, with models becoming 'occupied by distractors' during extended reasoning. The overthinking literature shows analogous degradation on math (Zhou et al., 2604.10739), scientific reasoning (Guan et al., 2603.14251), and conversational tasks (ThoughtTerminator's DUMB500).

The critical unsolved question is: through WHICH of the three counting-failure mechanisms does extended reasoning produce degradation? The geometric readout bottleneck is plausibly static—a structural property of the embedding space unlikely to change with reasoning length. But the active suppression MLP and the fragile attention routing compensation are dynamic, context-dependent mechanisms that extended reasoning could plausibly perturb. No existing work tests these differential predictions. Without this three-mechanism decomposition, the field treats 'counting failure under extended reasoning' as monolithic, risking interventions that target the wrong bottleneck.",
  "opportunity": "Garcia's geometric readout bottleneck (2605.03258) provides, for the first time, a clean invariant against which to measure the dynamic effects of extended reasoning. If |cos(count_dir, digit_output_row)| remains stable across reasoning budgets (256–8192 tokens) while attention routing compensation degrades and/or suppression MLP activation increases, we obtain a crisp mechanistic dissection that no prior work has attempted. This orthogonality stability measurement—tracking the cosine angle between count-encoding probe directions and output-head rows across the reasoning trajectory—is a novel diagnostic that directly tests whether extended reasoning operates through static geometric or dynamic routing/suppression channels.

Three previously isolated research threads converge to make this uniquely tractable:

(1) Counting-circuit characterization: Garcia (2605.03258), Datta et al. (2604.00778), and Repeated-Token Counting (2605.09239) provide the three-mechanism decomposition with specific, measurable targets—the cosine angle for mechanism #1, late-layer MLP activation patterns for mechanism #2, and logit-lens accuracy at layers ~20–26 for mechanism #3.

(2) Reasoning circuit analysis: Thinking Sparks (Park et al., 2509.25758, ICLR 2026) identifies reasoning-emergent attention heads in Qwen3-8B using EAP-IG and documents 'an inherent tension where complex reasoning comes at the cost of elementary computations.' Hu et al.'s Transcoder Adapters (2602.20904) provide a complementary methodology showing that only ~8% of reasoning-model changes are reasoning-specific (the rest being domain knowledge), suggesting the interference channel may be surprisingly narrow.

(3) Within-mode trajectory methodology: Probing the Trajectories of Reasoning Traces (2601.23163) provides a validated protocol for token-percentile truncation on Qwen3 models, directly applicable to tracking all three mechanisms across reasoning steps.

Critically, all three counting-failure mechanisms have been characterized on Qwen3 models—the same family where Thinking Sparks characterized reasoning circuits—creating a rare opportunity for cross-domain circuit interaction analysis on an already-characterized model family. Chen et al.'s 'Navigating by Old Maps' (2605.06076) cautions that circuits undergo 'Free Evolution' during parameter updates, making cross-context transfer of published characterizations unreliable; we mitigate this by re-running EAP-IG on our specific models and tasks rather than relying on prior characterizations.",
  "landscape": "The counting-failure mechanism literature has rapidly differentiated. Garcia ('The Right Answer, the Wrong Direction,' arXiv:2605.03258, May 2026) demonstrates across three model families (Pythia, Qwen3, Mistral; 0.4B–14B) that count-encoding directions are nearly orthogonal to digit-token output-head rows (mean |cos| = 0.016, all |cos| ≤ 0.032, statistically indistinguishable from random directions at p = 0.79). Linear probes recover counts with R² > 0.99 from layer 2 onward, but logit-lens accuracy peaks at only 23.4% (entity-mean position) to 41.6% (last-token position, layer 26). A 9-row output-head repair (36,864 params) reaches 60.7–100% on constrained prediction but 0% on autoregressive generation; LoRA Q/V attention routing (7.67M params) achieves 83.1% ± 7.2% in deployment by amplifying residual-stream count representation 24× at the final layer. The orthogonality worsens with scale: Qwen3-14B shows |cos| = 0.011 (0.57× random baseline). This establishes the geometric readout bottleneck as a static structural property. 'From Early Encoding to Late Suppression' (Datta et al., arXiv:2604.00778, April 2026) shows that late-layer MLPs (penultimate and final layers in LLaMA-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-3B) actively suppress correct character counts, constituting a distinct dynamic suppression mechanism. 'Repeated-Token Counting Reveals a Dissociation Between Representations and Outputs' (arXiv:2605.09239, May 2026) extends this on Llama-3.2 and Qwen2.5 (1.5B–7B): linear probes decode correct counts with R² > 0.99 at every post-embedding layer, but a format-triggered MLP block at ~88–93% depth overwrites the correct count. The suppression is format-sensitive (space-separated triggers; comma-separated rescues in larger models) and cross-architectural (consistent relative depth across Llama and Qwen). Dai & Fan ('Language models fail at extended rule following,' arXiv:2605.02028, May 2026) show 126 model variants fail at counting above model-dependent, syntax-sensitive thresholds, employing finite internal states that exhaust at predictable limits.

Word recovery research (arXiv:2603.10771) identifies early-layer in-group attention as critical for character reconstruction. The Spelling-out paper (EMNLP 2025 Findings, arXiv:2506.10641) shows embeddings encode only the first character well. CharBench (AAAI 2026, arXiv:2508.02591) provides large-scale character-level evaluation confirming tokenization's role. 'Say Anything but This' (Ayoobi et al., arXiv:2601.14658) demonstrates tokenizer non-uniqueness causes systematic reasoning failures. SubTokenTest (arXiv:2601.09089, January 2026) establishes the inverted U-shaped curve on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B with budget forcing, performance peaking at 1024–2048 tokens and degrading beyond.

On reasoning circuit analysis: 'Thinking Sparks!' (Park et al., arXiv:2509.25758, ICLR 2026) uses EAP-IG to demonstrate that post-training sparks functionally specialized attention heads in Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B, and Qwen3-8B. Distillation produces ~32 stable emergent heads (predominantly early-mid layers), SFT ~34 heads (mid-to-late layers), GRPO only 19–20 dynamically activated heads. Controllable 'think on/off' models (Qwen3-8B) do NOT possess dedicated 'thinking' heads; turning off reasoning triggers broader but less efficient compensatory heads. The paper documents 'an inherent tension where complex reasoning comes at the cost of elementary computations.' 'Transcoder Adapters for Reasoning-Model Diffing' (Hu et al., arXiv:2602.20904, February 2026) compares Qwen2.5-Math-7B vs. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B using interpretable transcoder adapters that approximate MLP computation differences, recovering 50–90% of reasoning accuracy gains. Only ~8% of adapter features are directly reasoning-related; 37% are domain knowledge; 5.6k features (2.4%) are necessary and sufficient for hesitation token production. This suggests reasoning-specific circuit changes may be narrower than previously assumed. 'From Reasoning to Answer' (Zhang et al., arXiv:2509.23676, EMNLP 2025) identifies mid-layer 'Reasoning-Focus Heads' via activation patching on DeepSeek-R1-Distill models. 'Understanding Reasoning in Thinking LMs via Steering Vectors' (Venhoff et al., arXiv:2506.18167) shows reasoning behaviors are mediated by linear directions.

'Navigating by Old Maps: The Pitfalls of Static Mechanistic Localization in LLM Post-Training' (Chen et al., arXiv:2605.06076, May 2026) demonstrates that circuits exhibit 'Free Evolution' during parameter updates—static circuits derived from current parameters may not guide future states. Their Circuit Distance, Circuit Stability, and Circuit Conflict metrics reveal systematic circuit transformation during fine-tuning. This raises a methodological concern about transferring Thinking Sparks' published head characterizations to new task contexts, which we address by re-running EAP-IG on our specific models and tasks.

On overthinking dynamics: 'Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute' (Gema et al., arXiv:2507.14417, TMLR 2025) constructs evaluation tasks where extending reasoning length deteriorates performance, including counting tasks with distractors where models become 'occupied by distractors' during extended reasoning—providing independent behavioral evidence of the phenomenon we study mechanistically. 'When More Thinking Hurts' (Zhou et al., arXiv:2604.10739) finds marginal utility turns negative beyond 12K tokens on AIME, with negative answer flips outnumbering positive by 7.55× at 16K tokens. ThoughtTerminator (Pu et al., arXiv:2504.13367) introduces DUMB500, revealing task-dependent overthinking—chat/task domains show negative token-accuracy correlation while math shows flat correlation. 'Mitigating Overthinking via Reasoning Path Deviation Monitoring' (Guan et al., arXiv:2603.14251) identifies high-entropy transition tokens as overthinking indicators.

'Probing the Trajectories of Reasoning Traces in Large Language Models' (arXiv:2601.23163) provides a validated token-percentile truncation protocol on Qwen3-4B/8B/14B. 'Think Deep, Not Just Long' (Chen et al., arXiv:2602.13517) introduces deep-thinking tokens where internal predictions undergo significant cross-layer revision. 'State over Tokens' (Levy et al., arXiv:2512.12777) reinterprets reasoning tokens as externalized computational state. 'Fluid Representations in Reasoning Models' (Kharlapenko et al., arXiv:2602.04843) shows progressive representation refinement during reasoning. 'Mitigating Overthinking via Manifold Steering' (Huang et al., arXiv:2505.22411) maps overthinking to a low-dimensional activation manifold.

No existing work connects the three-mechanism decomposition of counting failure (geometric bottleneck, active suppression, attention routing compensation) with extended reasoning dynamics to determine which mechanism mediates character-level degradation during thinking.",
  "inspired_by": "The convergence of three counting-failure mechanisms—Garcia's geometric readout bottleneck (static, |cos| ≤ 0.032), Datta et al./Repeated-Token Counting's format-triggered suppression (dynamic, late-layer MLPs), and the fragile attention routing compensation (dynamic, layers ~20–26)—creates the first opportunity for a differential diagnosis: extended reasoning plausibly perturbs dynamic mechanisms (#2 suppression, #3 routing) while leaving the static geometric bottleneck (#1) invariant, but this has never been tested. The orthogonality stability measurement (tracking |cos(count_dir, digit_row)| across reasoning trajectories) is a novel diagnostic that cleanly separates static from dynamic failure channels. Gema et al.'s independent behavioral confirmation of inverse scaling on counting under extended test-time compute (2507.14417), combined with Thinking Sparks' EAP-IG methodology on the exact Qwen3 model family, makes this both well-motivated and technically tractable. The narrow scope of reasoning-specific circuit changes revealed by Hu et al.'s transcoder adapters (~8% of features) suggests the interference channel may be surprisingly localized, further motivating circuit-level investigation.",
  "approach": "We adopt a phased approach structured around the three-mechanism decomposition of counting failure, with within-mode trajectory analysis as the PRIMARY evidence source (avoiding the between-mode confound identified by Thinking Sparks, where thinking vs. non-thinking modes engage fundamentally different head configurations).

**Hypotheses (with discriminating signatures):**
- H1 (Attention Routing Disruption): Extended reasoning co-opts the fragile attention routing compensation (layers ~20–26) that partially bridges the geometric readout bottleneck. As reasoning-emergent heads dominate the attention computation, the partial routing of count information toward output-compatible directions degrades. Signatures: (a) logit-lens accuracy at compensatory layers (20–26) decreases monotonically with reasoning budget, (b) EAP-IG edge weights for counting-related attention heads at those layers decline while reasoning-emergent head weights grow, (c) the geometric cosine |cos(count_dir, digit_row)| remains STATIC across reasoning budgets (confirming the bottleneck is structural, not dynamic), (d) suppression MLP activation is unchanged. This predicts degradation is character-task-specific because character tasks uniquely depend on the fragile routing channel.
- H2 (Suppression Amplification): Extended reasoning changes the upstream activation signature flowing into the format-triggered suppression MLP at 88–93% depth, causing it to fire more aggressively. The reasoning-generated context mimics the activation signature that triggers format-dependent suppression. Signatures: (a) correct character-level information persists in mid-layer residual streams even at 8192 tokens (R² remains high, consistent with the representation-output dissociation), (b) the suppression MLP's activation magnitude increases with reasoning budget for character tasks specifically, (c) logit-lens accuracy at compensatory layers is unchanged, (d) the geometric cosine remains STATIC, (e) format switching (comma-separated instead of space-separated) modulates the degradation curve, partially rescuing performance at extended budgets.
- H3 (Combined Degradation): Both H1 and H2 co-occur and potentially compound—attention routing degradation reduces compensation AND alters the activation distribution flowing into the suppression MLP, amplifying its firing. Signatures: both routing and suppression signatures present; causal ordering tested via targeted activation patching (patch compensatory heads to short-reasoning values while allowing suppression MLP to see full reasoning context, and vice versa).
- H4 (General Overthinking Null): Character-level degradation is NOT mechanistically distinct from general overthinking. The same answer-oscillation or path-deviation mechanisms that degrade math/science performance also degrade character-level performance, with no differential involvement of counting-specific circuits. Signatures: (a) count-encoding probe accuracy degrades at the same rate as control task probes (arithmetic, factual recall), (b) character-specific circuits (suppression MLP, compensatory attention routing) show NO differential activation changes, (c) standard overthinking indicators (entropy dynamics, answer oscillation) explain degradation equally across task types, (d) the geometric cosine remains STATIC (shared with all hypotheses).

**Phase 0: Behavioral Replication and Model Selection (weeks 1–2).** Replicate the inverted U-curve using budget forcing on character-level tasks (character counting, repeated-token counting, spelling from SubTokenTest) AND control tasks (arithmetic from MATH-500 Levels 1–3, factual recall from TriviaQA) on two models: (a) Qwen3-8B in thinking mode (primary model—Thinking Sparks characterized its reasoning heads, Garcia characterized counting geometry on the Qwen3 family), (b) Qwen3-14B in thinking mode (scale comparison—Garcia showed orthogonality is slightly worse at 14B: |cos| = 0.011, 0.57× random baseline). Token checkpoints: [256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]. Go/no-go decision tree: If both models show the inverted U-curve on character tasks → proceed as planned. If only one shows it → use that model as primary and note the scale-dependence. If NEITHER shows it → pivot to analyzing monotonic performance differences between character and control tasks under extended reasoning, testing whether the three mechanisms are modulated at all (even without producing an inverted U-curve), with appropriately reframed claims.

**Phase 1: Three-Mechanism Baseline Profiling Across the Reasoning Trajectory (weeks 2–5).** The PRIMARY evidence phase. Using the token-percentile truncation methodology from 'Probing the Trajectories of Reasoning Traces' (2601.23163), we profile all three mechanisms simultaneously at each token checkpoint:

(1a) Orthogonality stability diagnostic (NOVEL): At each checkpoint, extract hidden-state activations at every layer, train/apply linear probes to obtain count-encoding directions w_ℓ, and compute |cos(w_ℓ, e_k)| where e_k are the digit-token output-head rows (k = 0–9). Compare across checkpoints. Prediction under all dynamic hypotheses (H1–H3): |Δcos| < 0.01 (stability). If the cosine CHANGES significantly with reasoning length, this falsifies the 'static geometry' assumption and constitutes a finding of independent significance—meaning extended reasoning somehow modifies the geometric relationship between internal representations and the output head.

(1b) Suppression MLP profiling: Track the activation magnitude and pattern of the format-triggered MLP block at 88–93% depth (identified by Repeated-Token Counting) across reasoning checkpoints. Compare character vs. control tasks. Key measurement: does suppression MLP activation increase with reasoning budget for character tasks specifically?

(1c) Attention routing compensation profiling: Apply logit-lens at layers 20–26 (where Garcia showed partial count-to-output projection) at each checkpoint. Track logit-lens accuracy, the residual stream's projection onto digit-token rows, and probe R² at these layers. Key measurement: does the compensatory routing degrade with reasoning budget?

(1d) Control probing: Train linear probes for control-task features (intermediate arithmetic results, factual entity representations) at matched layers and checkpoints. This enables direct comparison of degradation rates: if character probes degrade faster or through different layers than control probes, it suggests character-specific mechanisms are involved.

Additionally, we measure the deep-thinking ratio (Chen et al., 2602.13517) at each checkpoint for character vs. control tasks to assess whether genuine reasoning effort differs across task types.

**Phase 2: Circuit Identification and Causal Verification (weeks 5–8).** Using EAP-IG (the same methodology employed by Thinking Sparks; requires ~2 forward passes + 1 backward pass), we perform three analyses:

(2a) Reasoning-circuit identification: Identify heads whose EAP-IG contribution to the residual stream grows most between the 256-token and 8192-token checkpoints. For Qwen3-8B, compare with Thinking Sparks' published characterization as a validation check (while heeding the Free Evolution concern from Chen et al., 2605.06076, by treating this comparison as suggestive rather than definitive).

(2b) Counting-circuit identification: Using EAP-IG, identify components causally responsible for character-level task performance at the 256-token checkpoint (where performance is near peak). Focus on: early-layer heads for character reconstruction, compensatory routing heads at layers 20–26, and the late-layer suppression MLP.

(2c) Cross-circuit interaction: Track how the reasoning-emergent components (from 2a) and counting-specific components (from 2b) interact across checkpoints. Targeted activation patching (via nnsight) for causal verification: (i) patch reasoning-emergent heads to their 256-token activation values while allowing counting circuits to process the full chain → if this restores character accuracy, reasoning heads causally mediate degradation (supports H1); (ii) patch the suppression MLP's input to its 256-token activation values while allowing reasoning heads to evolve → if this restores accuracy, suppression amplification is the causal pathway (supports H2); (iii) patch both → tests independence vs. compounding (H3 vs. H1/H2 alone).

**Phase 3: Format Modulation as Causal Lever (weeks 8–10).** Test the format-sensitivity of degradation under extended reasoning, leveraging Repeated-Token Counting's finding that comma-separated input rescues counting in larger models. Compare space-separated vs. comma-separated vs. digit-grouped formats at each budget checkpoint. If H2 (suppression amplification) holds, format switching should modulate the degradation curve—comma-separated inputs should partially rescue performance even at extended budgets by altering the activation signature entering the suppression MLP. If H1 (attention routing disruption) holds, format should be largely irrelevant because the failure occurs upstream of the suppression MLP. If H3 holds, format switching partially but incompletely rescues performance (suppression component rescued, routing component not). This phase provides an ecologically valid causal lever that complements the mechanistic patching in Phase 2.

Between-mode comparison as SECONDARY analysis: We compare thinking vs. non-thinking mode on Qwen3-8B with explicit acknowledgment that Thinking Sparks shows these modes engage fundamentally different head configurations. Rather than treating this as a clean ablation, we track whether the non-thinking mode's compensatory head set better preserves the fragile counting routing channel. This comparison is informative for understanding the breadth of reasoning's impact on counting circuits but is not load-bearing for hypothesis adjudication.

**Hypothesis Adjudication Framework:** We report discriminating evidence for each hypothesis using effect sizes and confidence intervals. For each mechanism (#1 geometry, #2 suppression, #3 routing), we report: (i) the measured change across reasoning budgets, (ii) whether the change is character-task-specific or shared with control tasks, (iii) whether activation patching causally implicates the mechanism. If H4 is supported (general overthinking, no character-specific mechanism), the contribution shifts to 'first three-mechanism profiling of counting failure dynamics under extended reasoning, showing all three mechanisms are invariant to reasoning length—useful for understanding that overthinking operates through a shared, task-general channel.'",

  "description": "We present the first mechanistic study decomposing how extended reasoning interacts with the three recently identified failure mechanisms underlying LLM character-level counting errors. The counting failure literature has converged on a critical decomposition: (1) a static geometric readout bottleneck where count-encoding directions are nearly orthogonal to digit-token output-head rows (|cos| ≤ 0.032; Garcia 2605.03258), (2) active format-triggered late-layer MLP suppression at 88–93% depth that overwrites correctly-encoded counts (Datta et al. 2604.00778; Repeated-Token Counting 2605.09239), and (3) fragile partial attention routing compensation at layers ~20–26 that bridges at most 41.6% of the geometric gap. We introduce a novel orthogonality stability diagnostic—tracking |cos(count_dir, digit_output_row)| across reasoning trajectories from 256 to 8192 thinking tokens on Qwen3-8B/14B—to test whether extended reasoning operates through static geometric or dynamic routing/suppression channels. Four competing hypotheses with distinct mechanistic signatures guide the investigation: attention routing disruption (H1—compensatory layers degrade), suppression amplification (H2—format-triggered MLP fires more aggressively), combined degradation (H3—both compound), and general overthinking null (H4—no character-specific mechanism). Within-mode trajectory analysis using token-percentile truncation, EAP-IG circuit identification, targeted activation patching, and format modulation experiments (leveraging the format-sensitivity of the suppression mechanism) provide converging causal evidence. By profiling all three failure mechanisms simultaneously across the reasoning trajectory and comparing character tasks against arithmetic and factual recall controls, we provide the first evidence for whether character-level degradation under extended reasoning reflects disruption of specific counting circuits or a general overthinking phenomenon—connecting the counting-failure mechanism literature with the overthinking dynamics literature for the first time.",

    "issue_1_garcia_integration": "CRITICAL STRUCTURAL CHANGE. Garcia's 'The Right Answer, the Wrong Direction' (2605.03258) is now the CENTRAL reference reframing the entire proposal. The geometric readout bottleneck (|cos| ≤ 0.032, R² > 0.99 probes vs. 23.4% logit-lens, 24× amplification via LoRA Q/V routing) establishes three mechanistically distinct failure channels: (1) static geometric misalignment, (2) dynamic suppression, (3) fragile attention routing compensation. This three-mechanism decomposition replaces the prior monolithic treatment of 'counting failure' and generates sharply discriminating experimental predictions. H2 (suppression routing amplification) is now explicitly reconciled with the orthogonality finding: the suppression MLP and geometric bottleneck are DIFFERENT mechanisms operating at different levels.   "landscape": "The counting-failure mechanism literature has rapidly differentiated. Garcia ('The Right Answer, the Wrong Direction,' arXiv:2605.03258, May 2026) demonstrates across three model families (Pythia, Qwen3, Mistral; 0.4B–14B) that count-encoding directions are nearly orthogonal to digit-token output-head rows (mean |cos| = 0.016, all |cos| ≤ 0.032, statistically indistinguishable from random directions at p = 0.79). CharBench (AAAI 2026, arXiv:2508.02591) provides large-scale character-level evaluation confirming tokenization's role. 'Say Anything but This' (Ayoobi et al., arXiv:2601.14658) demonstrates tokenizer non-uniqueness causes systematic reasoning failures. SubTokenTest (arXiv:2601.09089, January 2026) establishes the inverted U-shaped curve on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B with budget forcing, performance peaking at 1024–2048 tokens and degrading beyond.

The paper documents 'an inherent tension where complex reasoning comes at the cost of elementary computations.' 'Transcoder Adapters for Reasoning-Model Diffing' (Hu et al., arXiv:2602.20904, February 2026) compares Qwen2.5-Math-7B vs. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B using interpretable transcoder adapters that approximate MLP computation differences, recovering 50–90% of reasoning accuracy gains. This suggests reasoning-specific circuit changes may be narrower than previously assumed. 'From Reasoning to Answer' (Zhang et al., arXiv:2509.23676, EMNLP 2025) identifies mid-layer 'Reasoning-Focus Heads' via activation patching on DeepSeek-R1-Distill models. 'Understanding Reasoning in Thinking LMs via Steering Vectors' (Venhoff et al., arXiv:2506.18167) shows reasoning behaviors are mediated by linear directions.

'Navigating by Old Maps: The Pitfalls of Static Mechanistic Localization in LLM Post-Training' (Chen et al., arXiv:2605.06076, May 2026) demonstrates that circuits exhibit 'Free Evolution' during parameter updates—static circuits derived from current parameters may not guide future states. Their Circuit Distance, Circuit Stability, and Circuit Conflict metrics reveal systematic circuit transformation during fine-tuning. This raises a methodological concern about transferring Thinking Sparks' published head characterizations to new task contexts, which we address by re-running EAP-IG on our specific models and tasks.

On overthinking dynamics: 'Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute' (Gema et al., arXiv:2507.14417, TMLR 2025) constructs evaluation tasks where extending reasoning length deteriorates performance, including counting tasks with distractors where models become 'occupied by distractors' during extended reasoning—providing independent behavioral evidence of the phenomenon we study mechanistically. 'Mitigating Overthinking via Manifold Steering' (Huang et al., arXiv:2505.22411) maps overthinking to a low-dimensional activation manifold.

No existing work connects the three-mechanism decomposition of counting failure (geometric bottleneck, active suppression, attention routing compensation) with extended reasoning dynamics to determine which mechanism mediates character-level degradation during thinking.",

Token checkpoints: [256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]. Go/no-go decision tree: If both models show the inverted U-curve on character tasks → proceed as planned. If only one shows it → use that model as primary and note the scale-dependence. If NEITHER shows it → pivot to analyzing monotonic performance differences between character and control tasks under extended reasoning, testing whether the three mechanisms are modulated at all (even without producing an inverted U-curve), with appropriately reframed claims.

**Phase 1: Three-Mechanism Baseline Profiling Across the Reasoning Trajectory (weeks 2–5).** The PRIMARY evidence phase. Using the token-percentile truncation methodology from 'Probing the Trajectories of Reasoning Traces' (2601.23163), we profile all three mechanisms simultaneously at each token checkpoint:

(1a) Orthogonality stability diagnostic (NOVEL): At each checkpoint, extract hidden-state activations at every layer, train/apply linear probes to obtain count-encoding directions w_ℓ, and compute |cos(w_ℓ, e_k)| where e_k are the digit-token output-head rows (k = 0–9). (1b) Suppression MLP profiling: Track the activation magnitude and pattern of the format-triggered MLP block at 88–93% depth (identified by Repeated-Token Counting) across reasoning checkpoints. Compare character vs. control tasks. Key measurement: does suppression MLP activation increase with reasoning budget for character tasks specifically?

(1c) Attention routing compensation profiling: Apply logit-lens at layers 20–26 (where Garcia showed partial count-to-output projection) at each checkpoint. Track logit-lens accuracy, the residual stream's projection onto digit-token rows, and probe R² at these layers. Key measurement: does the compensatory routing degrade with reasoning budget?

(1d) Control probing: Train linear probes for control-task features (intermediate arithmetic results, factual entity representations) at matched layers and checkpoints. This enables direct comparison of degradation rates: if character probes degrade faster or through different layers than control probes, it suggests character-specific mechanisms are involved.

Additionally, we measure the deep-thinking ratio (Chen et al., 2602.13517) at each checkpoint for character vs. control tasks to assess whether genuine reasoning effort differs across task types.

**Phase 2: Circuit Identification and Causal Verification (weeks 5–8).** Using EAP-IG (the same methodology employed by Thinking Sparks; requires ~2 forward passes + 1 backward pass), we perform three analyses:

(2a) Reasoning-circuit identification: Identify heads whose EAP-IG contribution to the residual stream grows most between the 256-token and 8192-token checkpoints. For Qwen3-8B, compare with Thinking Sparks' published characterization as a validation check (while heeding the Free Evolution concern from Chen et al., 2605.06076, by treating this comparison as suggestive rather than definitive).

(2b) Counting-circuit identification: Using EAP-IG, identify components causally responsible for character-level task performance at the 256-token checkpoint (where performance is near peak). Focus on: early-layer heads for character reconstruction, compensatory routing heads at layers 20–26, and the late-layer suppression MLP.

(2c) Cross-circuit interaction: Track how the reasoning-emergent components (from 2a) and counting-specific components (from 2b) interact across checkpoints. **Phase 3: Format Modulation as Causal Lever (weeks 8–10).** Test the format-sensitivity of degradation under extended reasoning, leveraging Repeated-Token Counting's finding that comma-separated input rescues counting in larger models. If H1 (attention routing disruption) holds, format should be largely irrelevant because the failure occurs upstream of the suppression MLP. If H3 holds, format switching partially but incompletely rescues performance (suppression component rescued, routing component not). This phase provides an ecologically valid causal lever that complements the mechanistic patching in Phase 2.

Rather than treating this as a clean ablation, we track whether the non-thinking mode's compensatory head set better preserves the fragile counting routing channel. This comparison is informative for understanding the breadth of reasoning's impact on counting circuits but is not load-bearing for hypothesis adjudication.

Large reasoning models frequently waste resources by "overthinking" simple queries while failing to allocate sufficient compute to more complex problems. Signatures: (a) logit-lens accuracy at compensatory layers (20–26) decreases monotonically with reasoning budget, (b) EAP-IG edge weights for counting-related attention heads at those layers decline while reasoning-emergent head weights grow, (c) the geometric cosine |cos(count_dir, digit_row)| remains STATIC across reasoning budgets (confirming the bottleneck is structural, not dynamic), (d) suppression MLP activation is unchanged. This predicts degradation is character-task-specific because character tasks uniquely depend on the fragile routing channel.
- H2 (Suppression Amplification): Extended reasoning changes the upstream activation signature flowing into the format-triggered suppression MLP at 88–93% depth, causing it to fire more aggressively. The reasoning-generated context mimics the activation signature that triggers format-dependent suppression. Signatures: (a) correct character-level information persists in mid-layer residual streams even at 8192 tokens (R² remains high, consistent with the representation-output dissociation), (b) the suppression MLP's activation magnitude increases with reasoning budget for character tasks specifically, (c) logit-lens accuracy at compensatory layers is unchanged, (d) the geometric cosine remains STATIC, (e) format switching (comma-separated instead of space-separated) modulates the degradation curve, partially rescuing performance at extended budgets.
- H3 (Combined Degradation): Both H1 and H2 co-occur and potentially compound—attention routing degradation reduces compensation AND alters the activation distribution flowing into the suppression MLP, amplifying its firing. Signatures: both routing and suppression signatures present; causal ordering tested via targeted activation patching (patch compensatory heads to short-reasoning values while allowing suppression MLP to see full reasoning context, and vice versa).
- H4 (General Overthinking Null): Character-level degradation is NOT mechanistically distinct from general overthinking. The same answer-oscillation or path-deviation mechanisms that degrade math/science performance also degrade character-level performance, with no differential involvement of counting-specific circuits. Signatures: (a) count-encoding probe accuracy degrades at the same rate as control task probes (arithmetic, factual recall), (b) character-specific circuits (suppression MLP, compensatory attention routing) show NO differential activation changes, (c) standard overthinking indicators (entropy dynamics, answer oscillation) explain degradation equally across task types, (d) the geometric cosine remains STATIC (shared with all hypotheses).
